title: Квартира только для девочек  (Apartment for Girls Only)

segments.t: After looking around the modest flat, Max agrees to rent it, only for the landlady to tell him she rents exclusively to girls. Meanwhile, Chef Barinov shares a drink and wartime stories with Kirill Ilyich to restore peace. Listen to the Russian scene first, and then we will go through every line.
А зачем мне тогда квартиру показывали?
Так ты же деньги за просмотр заплатил.
Ну что, Кирилл Ильич, теперь мир?
Now let's go back through their conversation line by line and unpack the Russian phrasing.
'Well, how do you like my little apartment?' the hostess anchors the line on 'come on', while 'little apartment' completes the thought. Max answers right away.
'Alright, one can live here.' The grammar packs 'all right' and 'may' into a tight, idiomatic kitchen exchange.
'Who can live here?' In Russian, the idea of 'to whom' flows naturally into 'may' without extra filler words.
'I can live here.' In Russian, the idea of 'to me' flows naturally into 'may' without extra filler words. the hostess answers right away.
'You are not allowed to live here.' the hostess anchors the line on 'and', while 'one must not' completes the thought.
'But why am I not allowed?' The grammar packs 'but' and 'one must not' into a tight, idiomatic kitchen exchange.
'I only rent the apartment out to girls.' Here the Russian phrasing highlights 'I' before landing on 'I rent out'. Max answers right away.
А зачем мне тогда квартиру показывали?
'Then why did you show me the apartment?' The grammar packs 'and' and 'showed' into a tight, idiomatic kitchen exchange.
Так ты же деньги за просмотр заплатил.
'Because you paid the money for the viewing.' the hostess anchors the line on 'so', while 'to pay' completes the thought.
'And everything turned out so well.' Notice the reflexive suffix on the verb meaning 'turned out', turning the action back on the subject.
'They gave him a brand-new motorcycle.' Chef Barinov brings out the contrast between 'to him' and 'to give' in a few short words.
Ну что, Кирилл Ильич, теперь мир?

'Well then, Kirill Ilyich, is it peace now?' In Russian, the idea of 'come on' flows naturally into 'world' without extra filler words. Alright, let's hear the entire conversation one more time from start to finish.
А зачем мне тогда квартиру показывали?
Так ты же деньги за просмотр заплатил.
Ну что, Кирилл Ильич, теперь мир?

Max realizes the landlady tricked him out of his viewing fee, while Chef Barinov thinks he has sealed a truce with Kirill Ilyich. In the next scene, Grandpa Kirill adds one condition for Nagiyev, and Max recruits Katya for a clever scheme.
